fix_options.label: A. Upstream guard (taken by d555f2c)
fix_options.summary: Guard the class free hook call in archLoad() with 'archFree != NULL'.
fix_options.tradeoffs: none; the body is memSet to 0 afterwards as before
fix_options.maintainer_fit: it is his own commit d555f2c

notes: No patch: completely fixed. The hook-on-half-loaded-body residue is handled by patches 0001 (sub) and 0003 (dist), which adopt the protocol d555f2c implies: archLoad() performs the clean-up through the class free hook, so a loader must leave a body the hook accepts and must not free fields itself.

review_accuracy: accurate on mechanism, location and reproducer. Its 'Fix' line also asks to validate the archDomTerm() result unconditionally: for an in-range number this cannot fail in any class that has a matcher (archCmpltDomTerm, archHcubDomTerm, archMesh*DomTerm, archTleafDomTerm, archSubDomTerm, archDeco2DomTerm only reject numbers >= size), so it is an internal consistency check; patch 0002 keeps it as 'internal error (1)' in the same chain. The review missed that the debug check itself lets vnumnbr == 0 through (domnnbr = -1) and that a negative count reaches memAlloc in the loader.
first_pass_critique: Status, method and preferred option are right, and its diff is close to patch 0002. Shortcomings: it did not cite the in-tree precedent that settles the question (archDeco2ArchBuild, arch_deco2_build.c:604-615, already performs the same two checks unconditionally with the same messages); it reports the archDomTerm() failure as a user-facing 'invalid terminal number' although it is unreachable; it left the loader's count unchecked, so 'sub -1 ...' still reports a misleading 'out of memory (1)' and 'sub 0 ...' goes through memAlloc(0) before being rejected in Build (patch 0002 rejects both at 'bad input (1)', like archCmpltArchLoad's 'termnbr < 1'). Its option B is correctly marked weaker (does not protect SCOTCH_archSub).

fix_options.label: A. Unconditional checks in archSubArchBuild() plus count check in archSubArchLoad()
fix_options.summary: Lift the SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH1 guards (count, range, duplicate), require 1 <= vnumnbr <= orgtermnbr, fold the archDomTerm() result into the message chain as an internal error, and reject termnbr < 1 in the loader before allocating.
fix_options.tested: 32-bit and 64-bit ASan trees and SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL tree: repro/COR-03/run.sh (all cases rejected, no report), check_scotch_arch/_build/_deco, check_prog_atst/amk/amk_grf/acpl/gmap/gpart*, alloc-failure sweep
fix_options.tradeoffs: O(vnumnbr) compares per build (negligible); inputs that silently corrupted memory now fail; vnumnbr == 0 is now rejected (it never worked).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: exactly what he did for the derived routine archDeco2ArchBuild (arch_deco2_build.c:604-615, unconditional, same messages) and for user-controlled sizes in 7.0.17 (c5baef9 archHcubArchLoad bound, febaef7 negative edge values); archCmpltArchLoad's 'termnbr < 1' is the model for the loader check.

fix_options.label: B. Validate in archSubArchLoad() only
fix_options.summary: After loading the inner architecture, check the count against archDomSize() and detect out-of-range/duplicate numbers with a byte flag array; leave archSubArchBuild() debug-checked.
fix_options.tested: compiled and run on the ASan tree: messages correct for sub_range/sub_toomany/sub_dup/sub_zero (the remaining sanitizer reports are the un-fixed COR-04 free path, as expected for a validation-only change)
fix_options.tradeoffs: Does not protect SCOTCH_archSub()/SCOTCH_archSub Fortran (the API crash remains); duplicates the knowledge of terminal numbering; one more allocation per load.

cleanup_done: removed the two SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH1 blocks, the SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH2-only 'int o' and 'o =' wrapper around archDomTerm(); 'messptr' is now unconditional
notes: test_added is empty because src/check has no negative-test precedent (every test_*.c must succeed and the error library writes to stderr); a failing-call test would be a style departure, so the reproducers carry it. The manual (s_f.tex, 'sub') already states that the original architecture must have at least termnbr vertices; no doc change. Not patched (unrealistic): '2 * vnumnbr - 1' overflows Anum for vnumnbr > ANUMMAX/2, which requires an inner architecture of that many terminals and a file listing them.

review_accuracy: accurate; in my runs the 'double free' shows first as a heap-use-after-free READ in archFree (same root cause), and the 0xbebebebe class pointer reproduces exactly. Its 'Fix' line (publish on success, one owner per allocation, valid clasptr on every failure) is what patch 0001 does.
first_pass_critique: Evidence and location right. Its preferred option A (loader frees the inner Arch itself and NULLs it; Free tolerates NULL) works -- I built and ran it as alt COR-04-B -- but it is not the protocol the maintainer fixed into archLoad() with d555f2c ('Perform clean-up' through the class free hook) and which the tleaf loader already relies on (archTleafArchLoad leaves sizetab for archTleafArchFree on 'bad input (2)'); its option B (the body owns the inner Arch from allocation, the hook frees it exactly once), which it marked 'not tested' and 'more coupling', is the one consistent with the tree and is smaller. Its objection that 'Build() would need two modes' under B is wrong: publishing only on success is required by both options and the SCOTCH_archSub() path is unchanged. Its diff also left the chain-of-tree-blocks leak and the two debug-only error paths (see PS-COR-3).

extra_instances.location: src/libscotch/arch_sub.c:463-468 (SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH2 'internal error (1)' path frees treetab/termtab but not the matching structure)

fix_options.label: A. Body owns the inner Arch from its allocation; Free is the single clean-up (patch 0001)
fix_options.summary: archSubArchLoad() NULLs archptr/termtab on entry ('Assume nothing allocated yet', as archDeco2ArchLoad2 does), archInit()s the inner Arch and stores it in the body right after allocation, and never frees it itself: archLoad() frees it through archSubArchFree(), which skips NULL pointers. archSubArchBuild() sets the body fields only on success and frees all of its data on every error path (shared tree-block loop, 'else' chained under #ifdef SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH2 as in graph_coarsen.c:331).
fix_options.tested: see 'ran': 32/64-bit ASan trees, SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL tree, malloc-failure sweep, check_scotch_arch/_build/_deco, check_prog_atst/amk/amk_grf/acpl/gmap/gpart*, git am on a fresh clone
fix_options.tradeoffs: Relies on archLoad() calling the class hook on failure (it does since 6.0; d555f2c kept it); a reused Arch not passed through archInit() is covered by the explicit NULLing. No ABI change.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: matches d555f2c's intent (archLoad performs the clean-up), archInit()'s stated purpose (arch.c:130-132: zeroed body so class routines can test their pointers), archDeco2ArchLoad2's 'Assume nothing allocated yet' NULLing (arch_deco2_build.c/arch_deco2.c:146-148), archDecoArchFree/archTleafArchFree's NULL-tolerant frees, and his 'else' + '#endif' chaining (graph_coarsen.c:331).

fix_options.label: B. Loader cleans up after itself; Free tolerates NULL
fix_options.summary: Keep archExit()/memFree() of the inner Arch in archSubArchLoad() (after an archInit()), set archptr to NULL afterwards, NULL the fields on entry, make archSubArchFree() NULL-tolerant, and publish Build's fields only on success.
fix_options.tested: built into the ASan tree and run: sub_dup/sub_badtype/sub_badinner/sub_short/sub_var -> ret=1, 0 sanitizer hits; sub_ok loads
fix_options.tradeoffs: Works, two lines longer, two owners over the lifetime of the inner Arch (loader then body), and contradicts the hook-does-the-clean-up protocol that the other loaders follow.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: plausible but not his pattern: no loader in the tree frees what its Free hook will free.

fix_options.label: C. Build into a temporary ArchSub and copy on success
fix_options.summary: Load into a local ArchSub and memCpy it into the body only when everything succeeded.
fix_options.tested: untested: not written -- it still needs a NULL-tolerant archSubArchFree() because archLoad() calls the hook on the (zeroed) body, so it is A plus a copy

cleanup_done: removed the archExit()/memFree() block of archSubArchLoad(); removed the early field assignments of archSubArchBuild() (moved to the success path); the duplicated per-branch frees of Build's tail are replaced by one tree-block loop and one 'if (o != 0)' exit
notes: Ownership protocol applied to both meta-architectures (sub in 0001, dist in 0003): (1) the loader NULLs its pointer fields first; (2) each allocation is stored in the body as soon as it exists, after archInit() for an Arch; (3) the loader frees nothing on failure -- archLoad() calls the class free hook; (4) the hook skips NULL fields and honours ARCHFREE for the inner Arch; (5) archSubArchBuild() (also behind SCOTCH_archSub) frees everything it allocated and sets the body only on success. Groups handling deco/deco2 (COR-16) should note that archDeco2ArchLoad2 currently frees on its own 'fail:' label AND is freed again by archLoad(); under this protocol the label would go. No negative test added (no precedent in src/check).

review_accuracy: accurate; both fix directions it offers are valid, and 'allocate and free the inner Arch' is the one taken.
first_pass_critique: Status, evidence and option A are right and close to patch 0003. Three gaps: (1) its diff declares a new exported routine archDistArchFree without the SCOTCH_NAME_INTERN entry in module.h, so a SCOTCH_RENAME build would export an unprefixed symbol; (2) it does not make a loaded dist inherit the inner architecture's ARCHPART/ARCHVAR flags, although archDistArchBuild() copies flagval for that purpose: a loaded 'dist 2 varcmplt' would be handled as fixed-size by the mapper (patch 0003 ORs the inner flags into the outer, which is what Build does, and the archtrip run shows var=1); (3) it does not validate crloval (kgraphInit rejects crloval < 1 in debug mode, kgraph.c:98-101). Its 'ask the Scotch team' on A vs B is answered below.

fix_options.label: A. Allocate and own the inner Arch; add archDistArchFree(); Build borrows (patch 0003)
fix_options.summary: archDistArchLoad() NULLs archptr, rejects crloval < 1, allocates+archInit()s the inner Arch, stores it in the body before archLoad() so that the new archDistArchFree() (ARCHFREE-aware, NULL-tolerant, same shape as archSubArchFree) frees it on failure and on archExit(); on success the inner flags are inherited as archDistArchBuild() does; archDistArchBuild() masks ARCHFREE out; module.h gets the rename.
fix_options.tested: see 'ran'; 32/64-bit ASan, SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL, malloc-failure sweep, check targets, git am
fix_options.tradeoffs: Makes an undocumented file type loadable (it was already saveable by archDistArchSave); +1 internal routine; archDistArchBuild() (no caller) changes flag semantics only for ARCHFREE.
